detail.longDescription:
In an assignment for my Computer Networks class, I am tasked with using sockets to receive HTTP packets. This is my current code: import socket from socket import * import sys # In order to terminate the program serverSocket = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM) port = 2319 ip = 'localhost' # Prepare a server socket serverSocket.bind((ip, port)) serverSocket.listen(5) while True: try: #Establish the connection print('Ready to serve...') print(f"Get the webpage at: http://{ip}:{port}/SocketServerProgrammingLab/HelloWorld.html") connectionSocket, addr = serverSocket.accept() #This line will only run upon opening the webpage print(f"Connected to {addr}") connectionSocket.recv(1024) filename = "SocketServerProgrammingLab/HelloWorld.html" f = open(filename) outputdata = f.read() #Send on HTTP header line into socket connectionSocket.send("HTTP/1.1 200 OK
".encode()) #Send the content of the requested file to the client for i in range(0, len(outputdata)): connectionSocket.send(outputdata[i].encode()) connectionSocket.send("
".encode()) connectionSocket.close() except IOError: #Send response message for file not found connectionSocket.send("HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
".encode()) #Close client socket connectionSocket.close() serverSocket.close() sys.exit() #Terminate the program after sending the corresponding data And currently, when opening the URL in my browser, it is completely blank, regardless of what I put after the port. If I were to comment out the line connectionSocket.send("HTTP/1.1 200 OK
".encode()) then it would properly show the contents of the HTML file, but it would show that HTML file regardless of what I put after the port. Am I incorrectly sending HTTP signals to the client socket? Why does it either always show the contents of the HTML file or never show it?
